title: Credit Derivatives and Credit-Linked Notes

maps.specifics: Your formula card lists CLN as its final row. Know the CLN structure (funded, note investor bears credit risk), total return swaps, and the CDS mechanics from LO 27.g. LOs 31.f and 31.g are separately flagged as worth knowing.

selectors.name: CLN structure: funded, investor bears risk
selectors.what: A credit-linked note is a funded credit derivative: the investor pays the principal upfront, earns a coupon that includes the credit premium, and is repaid less any credit loss, so the note investor is the protection seller and the issuer is the protection buyer. Through an SPV the note is linked to the assets sold to the SPV, not to the sponsor; issued directly by an originator it also carries the issuer's credit risk.

selectors.name: Total return swap: bond owner and spread
selectors.what: The payer passes the total return on a bond (coupons plus gain or loss) to the receiver against floating plus a spread. The payer owns the bond, the receiver is in the position of having borrowed at floating plus spread, and the spread compensates the payer for the risk that the receiver defaults when the bond has fallen; it is similar to a repo.

selectors.name: CDS mechanics and settlement
selectors.what: The CDS buyer pays the spread (quarterly in arrears is standard) until maturity or a credit event, and the seller pays L(1 - R) on a credit event (failure to pay, restructuring, bankruptcy). Settlement is by physical delivery of bonds at face value or, now usually, cash with an ISDA auction setting the cheapest-to-deliver price. A CDS is not insurance: the buyer need not own the reference obligation, and it pays only on a credit event.

selectors.name: Synthetic CDO valuation, compound and base correlation
selectors.what: Valuing a synthetic CDO tranche by the spread payments approach and the one-factor Gaussian copula, and the two implied correlations: compound (tranche) correlation prices an individual tranche, base correlation prices the 0 to a_q tranche; compound shows a smile and base a skew.
selectors.theory: Breakeven spread s = C/(A + B), where A is the PV of the premium on the expected outstanding tranche principal, B the PV of the accrual on defaults and C the PV of the expected tranche losses; for a fixed running spread the upfront is C - s x (A + B). The copula gives the conditional default probability Q(t | F) = N((N^-1[Q(t)] - sqrt(rho) x F) / sqrt(1 - rho)) with Q(t) = 1 - exp(-lambda t) from the index spread. Higher correlation lowers the risk of the equity tranche and raises that of senior tranches; with R = 40% the correlation is the only unknown that implied correlation solves for.

selectors.name: Process of valuing a CDS
selectors.source: Vardeez: 'Know the PROCESS only; exam calculations can be lengthy' on CR-13 b
selectors.what: The process of valuing a CDS with credit risk exposure accounted for: equate the PV of expected spread payments plus accrual to the PV of expected payoff, using risk-neutral default probabilities implied from bond prices or CDS quotes; the steps rather than the arithmetic.
